name: M15 lag-one serial-dependence transition response batch

source_references.citation: Bianco and Renò (2006), Dynamics of intraday serial correlation in the Italian futures market, Journal of Futures Markets 26, 61-84
source_references.supports: Opened publisher abstract studies FIB30 futures in 2000-2002. It reports mostly negative correlation below 20 minutes, mainly bid-ask bounce, but positive correlation in high and unexpected-volatility regimes. It does not test this rolling rule, FX, costs, or tradability.

source_references.citation: Li, Giraitis and Sucarrat (2025), Are Intraday Returns Autocorrelated?, Queen Mary University of London Working Paper 987
source_references.supports: Opened full working paper tests six FX pairs in 2017-2018 with methods robust to non-stationary zero-return periodicity. Lag-one dependence is weak and erratic at one minute and generally absent in weekly 15-minute windows. This is adverse boundary evidence, not support for profitability.

research.evidence_summary: Primary evidence establishes that intraday serial dependence can be horizon- and volatility-dependent, while recent robust FX evidence is strongly adverse at 15 minutes. The local 12-pair threshold, response mappings and horizons are an original compact falsification with an expected null, not a claimed edge.

feasibility.rationale: Uses causal completed M15 closes, prior ATR, supported fills/stops and same-day exits. Rolling-correlation and result-ledger compatibility remain unconfirmed by V2.

market.base_timeframe: M1 aggregated to completed London-aligned M15 bars
market.session: Weekday signals at completed London M15 bars ending 09:00 through 13:45; every exit due no later than 15:00

data.frequency: Interval-start M1 OHLC aggregated into Europe/London wall-clock M15 bars
data.minimum_history: Fifteen consecutive valid completed M15 closes ending at signal time plus sufficient valid observed M15 true ranges for ATR96 through t-1
preprocessing: Aggregate M1 candles to completed London M15 OHLC without forward filling; any absent, duplicate or invalid M1 candle invalidates its M15 bar and the 15-close signal union
Valid OHLC is finite and positive with high>=max(open,close), low<=min(open,close), and high>=low
Compute fourteen M15 log close returns from fifteen consecutive valid completed M15 closes
Compute current and one-bar-prior ordinary Pearson lag-one correlations over exactly twelve adjacent-return pairs as defined in math
Compute observed-sequence M15 true range and Wilder ATR96 through t-1; routine earlier elapsed gaps remain represented, but the 15-close event union must be physically consecutive
Use IANA Europe/London rules and canonical UTC storage
dependencies: V2 causal M1-to-M15 aggregation and boundary handling
V2 resolved signal-time spread, commission and slippage
limitations: The local ordinary Pearson statistic is not Li et al.'s robust inference procedure
Twelve pairs are noisy and threshold choice is unvalidated
Bid-ask bounce, zero-return periodicity and one extreme pair can dominate
Recent primary FX evidence is adverse at 15 minutes
Six correlated symbols/four cells are not independent

hypothesis.behavior: A first transition from neutral to strongly positive or negative lag-one M15 return dependence may briefly favor the regime-consistent mapping or its symmetric inverse over the next 30-60 minutes.
hypothesis.mechanism: Positive dependence can reflect gradual information incorporation while negative dependence can reflect liquidity reversal or bid-ask bounce; the inverse mapping tests whether a noisy local estimate reverses those interpretations.
works_when: The transition identifies a real temporary dependence state rather than estimation noise
The response persists beyond executable signal-close fills and costs
fails_when: The modern robust FX null dominates
A single return pair or zero process creates spurious extremes
Path-family overlap explains any apparent result
falsifiable_predictions: Both hold cells for one response mode are positive under normal and doubled costs
The 60-minute center is positive in both fixed UTC development halves and at least three symbols per half
Both cells survive center-derived common five-date removal
Event overlap reporting does not reveal that all gains are concentrated in R010, R014 or R017 intersections

definitions.name: m15_log_returns
definitions.formula: r_k=ln(C_k/C_{k-1}) for the fourteen consecutive completed M15 intervals ending at signal bar t
definitions.timing: Known only after completed t close

definitions.name: current_lag1_correlation
definitions.formula: rho_current=Corr((r_{t-11},...,r_t),(r_{t-12},...,r_{t-1})) using ordinary sample Pearson correlation over 12 ordered pairs

definitions.name: prior_lag1_correlation
definitions.formula: rho_prior=Corr((r_{t-12},...,r_{t-1}),(r_{t-13},...,r_{t-2})) using ordinary sample Pearson correlation over 12 ordered pairs
definitions.timing: One completed M15 interval behind current statistic

definitions.name: dependence_transition
definitions.formula: +1 iff abs(rho_prior)<0.30 AND rho_current>=0.30; -1 iff abs(rho_prior)<0.30 AND rho_current<=-0.30; otherwise 0; undefined correlation means 0
definitions.timing: Known at completed t close; direct extreme-to-opposite-extreme flips cannot trigger

definitions.name: latest_return_sign
definitions.formula: s=+1 iff r_t>0; s=-1 iff r_t<0; s=0 otherwise
definitions.timing: Known at completed t close; s=0 suppresses entry

definitions.name: regime_consistent_side
definitions.formula: s when dependence_transition=+1; -s when dependence_transition=-1; 0 otherwise

definitions.name: atr96_prior
definitions.formula: Wilder ATR96 over valid observed London M15 true ranges through t-1
definitions.timing: Frozen before signal t; require finite positive

definitions.name: trade_side
definitions.formula: regime_consistent_side for REGIME_CONSISTENT and its negative for REGIME_INVERTED

entries.long_condition: eligible dependence transition AND nonzero latest return AND trade_side=+1 AND cell flat
entries.short_condition: eligible dependence transition AND nonzero latest return AND trade_side=-1 AND cell flat
entries.signal_time: Completed London M15 boundary ending 09:00 through 13:45 on a valid M1 interval, when signal time plus holding_minutes<=15:00
entries.execution_details: Enter at V2's supported executable signal-close fill derived from the final completed M1 boundary; if no executable signal-close quote/fill exists, skip the event and report the suppression. V2 applies resolved/fallback spread, commission and slippage. Entry candle cannot trigger the stop; management starts next M1.
entries.order_type: Market order at supported signal-close execution
restrictions: One open position per symbol per cell
All fifteen M15 closes in the signal union must derive from physically consecutive valid M1 candles
Require finite rho_prior and rho_current with strictly positive Pearson denominator products
Persistent same-side extremes and direct extreme sign flips cannot retrigger until rho first returns strictly inside abs(rho)<0.30
Signals on a non-trading holiday or early close are absent because the required physically consecutive valid M1 union and executable fill are absent; no calendar is inferred from missing OHLC

exits.stop_loss: The chart stop is one prior ATR from signal_close_bid: long=bid-atr96_prior and short=bid+atr96_prior. Long triggers on bid and short on executable ask; adverse gaps fill at the worse executable open with costs. The chart distance is a signal definition, not the R denominator.
exits.time_exit: Exit at the executable M1 close ending exactly signal_time plus holding_minutes. On a valid due bar STOP_LOSS resolves before TIME_EXIT. If the due bar/fill is unavailable, invalidate the complete affected cell: retain no P&L, trade count, equity change, bootstrap observation or robustness result for that cell, publish DATA_INTEGRITY_FAILURE, and do not substitute a forced price.
exits.maximum_holding: At most 60 minutes and never after 15:00 Europe/London
exits.end_of_session: Signals are admitted only when their valid due M1 close is at or before 15:00 Europe/London. A missing post-entry M1 through the due bar invalidates the complete affected cell rather than being force-closed; any still-open position is simulation-fatal for that cell and cannot contribute to results.

risk.position_sizing: Each cell owns an isolated portfolio. At entry, size from common pre-entry equity so the executable adverse stop-fill loss excluding commission/slippage equals 0.25%: long distance=chart_stop minus executable long entry ask; short distance=executable short entry bid minus chart_stop, using absolute positive distance. Skip if either executable entry or stop distance is invalid/nonpositive or size is unrepresentable. Commission/slippage remain costs in realized R; no state crosses cells.
risk.maximum_risk_per_trade: 0.25% current equity using executable entry-to-chart-stop price distance before commission/slippage; actual adverse-gap loss may exceed this risk
risk.gross_exposure_limit: Per cell at most six symbols and 1.50% aggregate initial executable stop-distance risk; no cap shared across four portfolios
risk.leverage: Use lower of executable-stop-risk size and V2 limits; skip unrepresentable size
risk.concurrent_positions: Within each cell one per symbol and six total; four cells independently track all state

experiment.baseline: 12-pair lag-one correlation/0.30 rising edge/chart one-ATR stop; REGIME_CONSISTENT; hold=60
robustness_tests: Report all four cells and the immutable pre-R023 inventory in reports/STRATEGY_THROUGHPUT_LEDGER.md dated 2026-11-05T15:11:35Z, plus the four fixed R023 cells
Report symbols and two fixed UTC development halves divided at the exact midpoint timestamp of the fixed development interval; a boundary close belongs to the first half
Double spread, commission and slippage individually

For each response mode, rank London dates by that mode's normal-cost 60-minute aggregate cell net R, remove the five highest dates from both holds of that mode, and require both normal/doubled net R positive

For each cell, form its eligible London-weekday daily net-R series including zero-trade dates; run 10000 circular five-date block-bootstrap resamples with seed 2026023 and report the two-sided 95% percentile interval for total net R; center lower bound must exceed zero
Mode advances only if hold=60 center and hold=30 neighbor both pass
Report positive/negative transitions, undefined-correlation windows, zero-latest-return suppressions, maximum single-pair contribution to centered covariance, and executable-fill suppressions

Report event counts and net R for intersections and complements versus R010 close-streak, R014 alternating-path and R017 efficiency-transition triggers without creating selectable filters; complements with fewer than 100 trades are non-informative and prohibit promotion
costs: Use resolved/fallback spread, commission and slippage at each fill
benchmarks: Opposite response mode on identical transitions
experiment.multiple_testing: The auditable selectable inventory is the 16 families/348 cells listed in reports/STRATEGY_THROUGHPUT_LEDGER.md at 2026-11-05T15:11:35Z plus this four-cell R023 batch, totaling 17 families/352 selectable cells. R008's two diagnostic rows and named prior studies/trials are reported as non-selectable multiplicity context, never counted as cells. Cross-batch promotion uses this frozen inventory; incomplete IDs prohibit confirmation and no best-cell/family rescue is permitted.
rejection_criteria: Reject mode unless both holds positive normal/doubled
Reject if center non-positive in either fixed UTC half or fewer than three symbols positive in either half
Reject if center fewer than 300 trades
Reject if center-derived five-date removal makes either cell non-positive
Reject if center 95% circular-bootstrap lower bound is not above zero
Reject if either informative path-family complement is non-positive after normal/doubled costs
Never access holdout without explicit authorization for separately frozen version

pseudocode: Maintain consecutive completed London M15 closes and prior-only observed-sequence ATR96.
At each eligible boundary compute fourteen log returns from fifteen consecutive valid closes.
Compute prior and current ordinary Pearson correlations over their exact twelve adjacent-return pairs; suppress zero denominators.
Trigger only strict-neutral to inclusive-extreme transitions and require nonzero latest return.
Map consistent/inverted response and enter flat cells at signal close.
From next M1 process stop before due exit; fail only affected cells.
Publish four cells plus overlap, robustness and complete-ledger rows.
required_libraries: existing V2 candle aggregation, timezone, cost, fill and R-accounting components
data_structures: Rolling centered sums for two twelve-pair Pearson correlations
edge_cases: either zero Pearson denominator suppresses event
direct extreme sign flip is suppressed
one invalid M1 candle invalidates its M15 bar and event union
adverse gap uses worse executable open
implementation.computational_requirements: One causal M1 pass per symbol with M15 aggregation, short rolling return buffers, ATR state and four isolated portfolios.
known_backtester_gaps: Queue waits for V2 rolling lag-one correlation, overlap-reporting, boundary/fill and result-ledger compatibility confirmation
